group_assessment.weighting: A retrospective two-sibling case series (consanguineous Saudi family) with a homozygous SLC18A2 canonical splice-donor variant, classified likely pathogenic on PVS1, PM2 and PP1 by in-silico prediction only; CSF neurotransmitters planned but not performed. Treatment response is caregiver and clinician observation without scales. No WWOX content; the two siblings are the useful datum because the same genotype gave different tolerability and course.

entries.proposition: Both siblings were first treated as epilepsy; EEG captured events without epileptiform activity in the younger and showed slowing without discharges in the older.
entries.snippet: Electroencephalogram (EEG) captured the clinical events without associated epileptiform activity, leading to discontinuation of antiseizure therapy.

entries.proposition: The older sibling received valproate, levetiracetam and clonazepam without benefit before the diagnosis.
entries.snippet: the patient was treated sequentially with multiple antiseizure medications, including valproic acid, levetiracetam, and clonazepam; however, no clinical improvement was observed

entries.proposition: CSF neurotransmitter analysis was planned but could not be performed for technical reasons.
entries.snippet: Although cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) neurotransmitter analysis was planned, it could not be performed due to technical limitations.

entries.proposition: The authors state CSF profiles may be normal in PKDYS2, limiting diagnostic sensitivity.
entries.snippet: prior studies have shown that CSF profiles may be normal in individuals with PKDYS2, thereby limiting its diagnostic sensitivity

entries.proposition: The splice-donor variant was classified likely pathogenic without functional validation.
entries.snippet: Although functional validation was not performed, the variant is considered causative based on its canonical splice-site location

entries.proposition: The authors summarise pramipexole as variably tolerated and effective across the two siblings (one improved, the other had dose-limiting dyskinesia and insomnia).
entries.snippet: In contrast, pramipexole demonstrated variable tolerability and efficacy.

entries.proposition: Same homozygous variant, different severity and treatment response in the two siblings.
entries.snippet: the two siblings in our report exhibited differential clinical severity and treatment response despite sharing the same homozygous SLC18A2 variant

entries.proposition: The authors concede the pramipexole benefit may reflect natural fluctuation.
entries.snippet: the observed improvement with pramipexole in one patient may partially reflect natural disease fluctuation

entries.proposition: Limits named by the authors: no functional validation, no CSF analysis, small sample, short follow-up.
entries.snippet: absence of functional validation, lack of cerebrospinal fluid neurotransmitter analysis, small sample size, and relatively short follow-up

entries.proposition: The authors cite another cohort with a dorsal brainstem and pons T2 hyperintensity with restricted diffusion; their own two patients had normal MRI.
entries.snippet: bilateral symmetric T2 hyperintensity and restricted diffusion involving the dorsal brainstem and pons
